item: The WAL starvation soak bounds the log by the time a checkpoint attempt took, not by a fixed byte ceiling
status: built (draft PR; folded into the shutdown-WAL change)
refs: PR #1475; coordinator 26 Oct 04:21: cause accepted (a fixed byte ceiling standing in for a time bound), fold into the shutdown-WAL PR, relative bound with each term named, the 300 ms fsync delay as the red-without; CI failure on the PR #1466 run (job test, 26 Oct 04:06Z)
summary: tests/test_wal_starvation_soak.py failed once on CI (round 2 of 3: 9,261,792 B of WAL against 6 x 1,048,576 = 6,291,456 B) with the code under it unchanged since 18 Oct; the property (a checkpoint completes while a producer is mid-scan, 10 in-scan releases, a success every round) held in all three rounds, only the ceiling failed. The writer appends 256 KiB every ~20 ms and the size read at the end of the scan is what arrived since the last TRUNCATE finished, which costs 3 to 4 fsyncs: the ceiling was a time bound. Reproduced in this container with strace-injected fsync delay (idle 0 to 796 KiB; 4 and 8 CPU burners did not reproduce; 100 ms gave 1.6 to 2.9 MiB; 300 ms gave 6,394,272 / 6,666,192 / 6,666,192 B with 1 attempt a round). The test now allows 6 x the checkpoint ceiling PLUS the writer's measured rate x the round's longest checkpoint attempt (headroom, in_flight and total printed on failure); the anti-vacuity checks stay. Four tests: the main property, the CI-round arithmetic pin, the never-truncated-log pin (about 11 MB against about 6.9 MB) and a real round with a 0.6 s attempt delay. Red-without: under the 300 ms fsync delay the old assertion fails and the new one passes on the same file. NOT shown: the runner's real fsync latency (nothing logs it); the mechanism reproduces the signature, it is not a measurement of that run.
